core_obligations: Set up a solid diagram for f|_U over a first-order thickening of T by T'.
Use formal unramifiedness of f to bound extensions into X by at most one.
Conclude at most one extension into U exists, i.e. f|_U is formally unramified.

proof_roadmap.step: Bound extensions into X via the uniqueness property of f.
Restrict the bound to extensions landing in U.

difficulty_reason: If f : X -> S is formally unramified, the restriction f|_U : U -> V to opens with f(U) inside V is formally unramified. The retained proof is the diagram argument written out: given a solid diagram with a first-order thickening T -> T' as in the definition, formal unramifiedness of f bounds the number of S-morphism extensions a' : T' -> X by at most one, and hence a fortiori there is at most one such extension landing in U. Retained author proof at lines 862-874.
